answer: At a wharf, agents auction space for quartz crates and ivory ceramic tiles. Each bidder locks a bond and earns future bidding weight only after independent shippers sign a delivery receipt checked against terminal scans. Extra identities start at zero weight; an attacker must move real cargo and risk collateral for every alias. A cartel could fake mutual receipts, and a rich actor can finance many shipments, so random dock audits and signer diversity limits remain necessary.
